description: A model scoring another model's output against a rubric. Useful for qualities code cannot check; biased and noisy, so it must be calibrated.
Named criteria with a description and a small scale. Specific criteria and few levels give more consistent scores.
Asking which of two answers is better. More reliable than absolute scores for choosing between variants; must run in both orders.
A judge preferring the first or second answer regardless of content. Detected by swapping the order.
A judge rating outputs from its own model family higher. Use a judge from another family.
Agreement corrected for chance: `(observed − expected) / (1 − expected)`. 1 is perfect, 0 is chance level, negative is systematic disagreement.
Comparing a judge's labels with human labels on the same outputs, and reading the disagreements, before trusting it.
